int_name: CHESTNUT ST & S SCHUYLKILL AVE W

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk and a high-visibility zebra crosswalk equipped with pedestrian signals. However, the multi-lane roadway and lack of a physical median refuge increase exposure for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Exposure
hazards.description: The multi-lane configuration increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a mid-point refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway area at the crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Separation
hazards.description: The buffer between the sidewalk and travel lanes relies on flexible delineator posts rather than a rigid physical barrier.
hazards.location_in_image: White bollards along the roadway edge

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the crossing to reduce the total crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add street trees along the sidewalk to provide a vertical buffer and visually narrow the roadway to encourage slower speeds.

result.summary: The image shows a well-maintained bridge environment with a wide sidewalk and a buffered green bike lane. A marked zebra crosswalk with a tactile curb ramp is present, though the crossing distance across multiple lanes lacks a central refuge island.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic and a bike lane without a mid-crossing refuge island.

hazards.name: Soft protection for bike lane
hazards.description: The bike lane is separated only by flex posts, which do not provide physical protection from motor vehicle incursions.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the sidewalk, separating the bike lane from travel lanes

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and reduce exposure.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing lights to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled crossing.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals, providing a basic level of safety. However, the wide roadway creates a long crossing distance without a median refuge, increasing pedestrian exposure to multi-lane traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to spend a significant amount of time in the conflict zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, across the main roadway

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide street in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane or shoulder to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection equipped with marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and a small refuge island. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment is dominated by multiple travel lanes and a channelized right-turn lane that increase crossing distances and potential vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to traffic for a significant duration due to the width of the multi-lane roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Main crossing across the multi-lane street

hazards.name: Channelized Right Turn
hazards.description: The slip lane design allows for higher vehicle turning speeds, increasing the risk of conflict with pedestrians crossing to the refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection foreground

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Implement a signal timing change that gives pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

interventions.title: Tighten Turn Radii
interventions.description: Redesign the channelized turn to have a tighter radius, forcing vehicles to slow down significantly before the pedestrian crossing.
